Pearls are delicate, so gentle care is key. After each wear, simply wipe them down with a dry, soft cloth to remove oils and dirt. That's often all they need.For deeper cleaning, use lukewarm water with mild dish soap and a soft cloth—but never submerge pearls, as water can damage them and weaken the string. If your pearls are set in metal like a ring or earrings, you can carefully clean the metal band with a cotton swab dipped in jewelry cleaner, just keep it away from the pearls themselves.Avoid ultrasonic or steam cleaners, heat, harsh chemicals, perfumes, and lotions. Store them flat in a soft box, separate from other pieces. Put them on last after your makeup and hair, and take them off first before bed to protect them from oils and cosmetics.With that routine, your pearls will stay beautiful for years. See our full pearl care guide for more details.

The white gold setting is durable, and at 0.66" long it's a refined size that works with most outfits. Ethiopian opal is relatively delicate though—it's softer than diamonds and can be sensitive to temperature changes and moisture—so you'd want to remove it before showering or swimming, and avoid bumping it against hard surfaces. If you're after something you can truly wear daily without worrying, the Black Ethiopian Opal 18k Yellow Gold Over Sterling Silver Pendant sits lower in price and pairs the same beautiful stone with a protective gold-over-silver setting.
